web.title: Marble Relief of Three Diners – Johns Hopkins Archaeological Museum
evidence: The page confirms that 'banquet scenes did not become a popular decorative motif in Roman funerary art until the first century C.E.' and discusses a Roman marble relief fragment depicting diners in a funerary context, but does not connect this to Statius's Silvae specifically.

web.title: Category: Ancient Roman funerary reliefs – Wikimedia Commons

web.title: What Do We Know About the People Buried in the Royal Cemetery? – Expedition Magazine (Penn Museum)
evidence: The article (by J. Reade, the likely source cited as 'JR94' in the Wikipedia article) places RT.1236 first in the stratigraphic sequence of royal tombs, directly implying it is the earliest. However, it does not explicitly call it 'the largest' tomb structure, and the relevant passage discusses relative chronological sequence rather than physical size.

web.title: Royal Cemetery at Ur – Madain Project
evidence: Directly states that tomb PG 1236 "is regarded as the largest and probably the earliest of the royal structures, dated to circa 2600 BCE" and links it to A-Imdugud via an inscribed seal. Fully matches the claim.

web.title: Ur-Pabilsag – Wikipedia
evidence: States that A-Imdugud is "known from grave PG 1236, which is the largest and probably the earliest tomb structure at the Royal Cemetery at Ur," corroborating the claim word-for-word, and cites a 1994 source tagged 'JR94' (likely Julian Reade 1994).

title: Bellsmyre
claim: Much of the remaining publicly owned housing under landlord Scottish Homes was transferred to the Bellsmyre Housing Association in 1992.
wikiWarnings: no counterpart article on the larger language editions

queries: "Bellsmyre" AND "1992" AND "bellsmyre housing association" AND "scottish homes"

web.title: Bellsmyre Housing Association – Sustainable Homes | Flexible Services & Vibrant Communities
evidence: "Bellsmyre Housing Association was founded in September 1992 with an initial housing stock of 150 properties following a stock transfer from Scottish Homes." Directly confirms the 1992 date and the Scottish Homes stock transfer, though it notes only 150 initial properties rather than characterising the transfer as 'much of the remaining' stock.

web.title: Bellsmyre Housing – West Dunbartonshire SSP Pipeline
evidence: "Bellsmyre Housing Association was founded in September 1992 with an initial housing stock of 150 properties following a stock transfer from Scottish Homes." Corroborates the 1992 transfer from Scottish Homes, apparently mirroring the association's own text.

web.title: Housing association 'no longer represents the people' says former committee member – Source
evidence: The article notes that BHA celebrated its 25th anniversary in September 2017 (consistent with a 1992 founding) and references Scottish Homes' involvement in the transfer, but does not explicitly state the year 1992 or characterise the scale of the transfer.

title: Al-Fatat SC
claim: It fields teams in several sports, and it was one of the founding members of the Kuwaiti Women's League football tournament in 2017.
wikiWarnings: 1 {{cn}}-family tag(s) found in wikitext but 2 rendered on page — same-article matching falls back to section-only

web.title: Kuwait FA on Twitter – انطلاق دوري كرة القدم النسائية الأربعاء #KuwaitFA
evidence: This is the sole primary source cited by the Kuwaiti Women's League Wikipedia article for the league's 2017 founding. It is a Kuwait FA official tweet announcing the start of the women's football league in October 2017. It may list participating clubs (potentially including Al-Fatat), but as a social media post it cannot be fully evaluated for exact wording without direct access, and Twitter/X posts have limited stability as citations.

web.title: Kuwaiti Women's League – Wikipedia
evidence: The Wikipedia article on the Kuwaiti Women's League lists Al-Fatat SC among the clubs in the league and states it was founded in 2017, implying Al-Fatat was a founding participant. However, it does not use the phrase 'founding member' explicitly, and Wikipedia itself is not a valid WP:RS source.

web.title: Success Against All Odds in Kuwait – FIFA Inside
evidence: This FIFA article confirms Al Fatat Club's participation in Kuwait's women's football league and mentions their championship win, but it focuses on the futsal league and does not explicitly state that Al-Fatat was a founding member of the Kuwaiti Women's League in 2017.

title: Knytt Underground
claim: Underground was Nifflas' biggest project at the time of its release, encompassing the biggest world and the most characters, sub-quests and secrets of any of his games thus far.

web.title: Knytt goes Underground, emerges on PS3, Vita, and more this year – Engadget
evidence: Contains a direct quote from Nifflas: "Knytt Underground is the biggest game I've ever developed," and notes it allows for "the biggest game I ever developed." This supports the 'biggest project' portion of the claim in Nifflas' own words at announcement time, but does not specifically enumerate 'biggest world,' 'most characters,' 'sub-quests,' or 'secrets' as the article's claim does.

web.title: Knytt Underground | Nicklas Nygren Wiki | Fandom
evidence: The Fandom wiki reproduces the claim verbatim: "Underground was Nifflas' biggest project at the time of its release, encompassing the biggest world and the most characters, sub-quests and secrets of any of his games thus far." However, it appears to be user-generated content without a cited primary source for this specific statement.

web.title: Wobble Reviews – Review: Knytt Underground (2012, PS3)
evidence: States "Underground is far larger than Nifflas' previous Knytt games and also the first to focus on story in a significant way," supporting the 'biggest world' aspect, but does not address most characters, sub-quests, or secrets specifically.
